title: Week 1 — Basic Terminology and Concepts
subtitle: Terminology · Fiqh vs Uṣūl · Scholars · Indicators
description: Master the foundational terminology of uṣūl al-fiqh: the definitions of fiqh, uṣūl, dalīl, and the roles of mujtahid, faqīh, mufti, muqallid, and ʿāmmī.
source: Islamic Legal Theory I course material.

questions.q: A student says: “Uṣūl al-fiqh studies the individual rulings assigned to actions, such as prayer being obligatory.” Which correction best matches the course material?
options: That is the subject matter of fiqh; uṣūl al-fiqh studies multiple-case indicators and the principles for deriving rulings.
That is the subject matter of uṣūl al-fiqh; fiqh studies only Arabic grammar.
Both sciences study only individual rulings.
Neither science studies rulings or indicators.

questions.q: A verse says, “Establish the prayer.” In the course terminology, this is an example of:
Which statement best defines a dalīl according to the material?
options: That which, when properly reasoned, can lead to a sacred law ruling, whether probabilistic or non-probabilistic
A ruling that applies only to devotional acts
A scholar who follows another scholar

questions.q: Knowledge of fiqh indicators means merely memorizing the names and definitions of the indicators.
A general rule states that a Qurʾānic or Prophetic command indicates obligation unless contextual evidence indicates otherwise. This is an example of:
options: Knowledge of the conditions of a mujtahid
The subject matter of devotional acts

questions.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Fiqh — multiple-case indicators; Uṣūl al-fiqh — individual rulings
Fiqh — sacred law rulings related to actions; Uṣūl al-fiqh — multiple-case indicators and rules of deduction
Fiqh — only worship; Uṣūl al-fiqh — only financial contracts
Fiqh — Arabic language; Uṣūl al-fiqh — hadith criticism

questions.q: A specialist deduces sacred law rulings from specific-case indicators. What is this specialist called?
A faqīh is described as a specialist who knows sacred law rulings deduced from specific-case indicators.
In the context of fiqh, “jumhūr” means:
options: The greater number of schools that hold an opinion on a particular fiqh case; the schools may vary from case to case

questions.q: In the context of uṣūl al-fiqh, “jumhūr” is used in the material as a synonym for:
options: Non-Ḥanafī jurists / mutakallimūn / Shāfiʿiyyah in this technical context

questions.q: Which activity belongs to fiqh’s theme of muʿāmalāt rather than ʿibādāt?
Name the two broad themes of fiqh identified in the material.
What is the term for a non-specialist in sacred law?
The material says that “Shāfiʿiyyah” has exactly the same scope in fiqh and uṣūl al-fiqh.
According to the book’s alternative definition, uṣūl al-fiqh is:
options: Knowledge of rules for deducing sacred law rulings from specific-case indicators
Knowledge of the individual rulings assigned to actions
Knowledge of the biographies of the great jurists

questions.q: Based on the two definitions of uṣūl al-fiqh, the book concludes that “multiple-case indicators” and “rules” are synonymous.
Which of the following is NOT one of the three components of the first definition of uṣūl al-fiqh?
options: Knowledge of multiple-case indicators of sacred law rulings
Knowledge of how to utilize these indicators in deducing rulings from specific-case indicators
Knowledge of the conditions required in a mujtahid-specialist
Knowledge of the history of every fiqh school

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a dalīl ijmālī (multiple-case indicator)?
options: The rule that an order to do an action indicates obligation unless there is contextual evidence to the contrary
A specific verse about the fast of Ramadan
A specific ruling on a sale contract

questions.q: In the course material, “sharʿ” refers to:
options: Rulings issued only by the Companions

questions.q: What word does the material give as a synonym of “sharʿ”?
How does the material suggest translating “ḥukm sharʿī”?
A “mufti” (jurisconsult) is best described as:
options: A specialist who follows a mujtahid
A specialist who deduces rulings from specific-case indicators and responds to laypeople’s questions on sacred law rulings
A specialist who only knows multiple-case indicators

questions.q: A “muqallid” (imitator/follower) is:
options: One who follows a mujtahid who deduces rulings from specific-case indicators
One who deduces rulings from specific-case indicators
A scholar who compiles books on legal theory

questions.q: An “uṣūlī” (legal theorist) is a specialist who knows:
options: Multiple-case indicators, how to utilize them in deducing rulings, and the conditions required in a mujtahid
Only the individual rulings of devotional acts
Nothing beyond the names of the schools
Only the Arabic grammar of the Qurʾān

questions.q: Which list contains only themes of devotions (ʿibādāt)?
options: Personal hygiene and purity (ṭahārah), mandatory almsgiving (zakat), pilgrimage (ḥajj)

questions.q: Which of the following is a crime-related theme within muʿāmalāt according to the material?
Which of the following is NOT listed as a major theme of uṣūl al-fiqh?
options: Resolving seeming conflict of sacred law indicators

questions.q: In the technical context of uṣūl al-fiqh, what term is used for Ḥanafī jurists, in contrast to the mutakallimūn?
Al-Risāla, listed among the classical works on uṣūl al-fiqh, was written by:
In the context of uṣūl al-fiqh, a “Shāfiʿī” jurist may be affiliated with the Mālikī, Ḥanbalī, or Ẓāhirī schools, since the term means non-Ḥanafī.
